start_here: Say to your AI: "Was event msg_1srOsB4mXhCqCVwAxYRNnpFZhb3 on my Resend webhook 00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000011 a hard bounce?", naming the held key. It runs tool:read-a-webhook-event and answers {"id":"msg_1srOsB4mXhCqCVwAxYRNnpFZhb3","type":"email.bounced","created_at":"2026-11-22T13:13:02.348Z","status":"failed","email_id":"00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000031","bounce":{"type":"Permanent","sub_type":"General"}}
no_lists_because: It keeps no list of yours: it reads one event your email-sending account sent to one webhook and writes nothing.
instructions: 1. Connect your Resend account once, so its key is held in your vault under a name of yours (a key with full access). The key is never typed into the request.
2. Find the event's id (msg_...) with tool:list-webhook-events, and the webhook's id with tool:list-resend-webhooks.

3. Say to your AI: "Read event <msg id> of my Resend webhook <id>", and give the held key's name. It calls tools:run with tool tool:read-a-webhook-event and {"key_name": "<that name>", "webhook_id": "<id>", "event_id": "<msg id>"}.
4. Read type, time, status and email_id. For a bounce, bounce.type says Permanent (the address will not take mail) or Temporary (try again later). Addressees, the subject and the key are never shown.
